events.label: Watson and Holmes are associated with three cases during July after Watson's marriage

events.label: Watson and Percy Phelps are associated during school-days

Percy Phelps obtains a good appointment at the Foreign Office through his uncle's influence
Percy Phelps writes a letter to Watson asking him to bring Holmes down to see him

communicates.speaker: percival_phelps
communicates.content: I have no doubt that you can remember "Tadpole" Phelps, who was in the fifth form when you were in the third. It is possible even that you may have heard that through my uncle's influence I obtained a good appointment at the Foreign Office, and that I was in a situation of trust and honour until a horrible misfortune came suddenly to blast my career. In the event of your acceding to my request it is probable that I shall have to narrate them to you. I have only just recovered from nine weeks of brain-fever, and am still exceedingly weak. Do you think that you could bring your friend Mr. Holmes down to see me? I should like to have his opinion of the case, though the authorities assure me that nothing more can be done. Do try to bring him down, and as soon as possible. Assure him that if I have not asked his advice sooner it was not because I did not appreciate his talents, but because I have been off my head ever since the blow fell. Now I am clear again, though I dare not think of it too much for fear of a relapse. I am still so weak that I have to write, as you see, by dictating. Do try to bring him.

events.label: Watson and Holmes meet in Holmes's rooms as Holmes works on a chemical investigation
Holmes tests a solution with litmus paper and it turns crimson
Holmes writes several telegrams and hands them to the page-boy
Watson hands Holmes the letter and Holmes reads it

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: It does not tell us very much, does it? Hardly anything. And yet the writing is of interest. But the writing is not his own. Precisely. It is a woman's. No, a woman's, and a woman of rare character. You see, at the commencement of an investigation it is something to know that your client is in close contact with some one who, for good or evil, has an exceptional nature. My interest is already awakened in the case.

communicates.speaker: percival_phelps
communicates.content: I won't waste your time. I'll plunge into the matter without further preamble. I was a happy and successful man, Mr. Holmes, and on the eve of being married, when a sudden and dreadful misfortune wrecked all my prospects in life.

events.label: Percy Phelps describes his Foreign Office career and his uncle's trust

communicates.speaker: percival_phelps
communicates.content: I was, as Watson may have told you, in the Foreign Office, and through the influences of my uncle, Lord Holdhurst, I rose rapidly to a responsible position. When my uncle became foreign minister in this administration he gave me several missions of trust, and as I always brought them to a successful conclusion, he came at last to have the utmost confidence in my ability and tact.

events.label: Lord Holdhurst gives Percy a new commission of trust involving the treaty

communicates.speaker: lord_holdhurst
communicates.content: This is the original of that secret treaty between England and Italy of which some rumours have already got into the public press. It is of enormous importance that nothing further should leak out. The French or the Russian embassy would pay an immense sum to learn the contents of these papers. They should not leave my bureau were it not absolutely necessary to have them copied. You have a desk in your office? Then take the treaty and lock it up there. I shall give directions that you may remain behind when the others go, so that you may copy it at your leisure without fear of being overlooked. When you have finished, relock both the original and the draft in the desk, and hand them over to me personally to-morrow morning.

events.label: Phelps says that all of his people had been shown over the office

communicates.speaker: percival_phelps
communicates.content: Oh, yes, all of them had been shown over it.

events.label: Holmes says the questions are irrelevant if no one was told about the treaty

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Still, of course, if you said nothing to any one about the treaty these inquiries are irrelevant.

events.label: Holmes asks about the commissionnaire

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Do you know anything of the commissionnaire?

events.label: Phelps says the commissionnaire is an old soldier

communicates.speaker: percival_phelps
communicates.content: Nothing except that he is an old soldier.

events.label: Holmes asks what regiment the commissionnaire served in

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: What regiment?

events.label: Phelps says the commissionnaire was in the Coldstream Guards

communicates.speaker: percival_phelps
communicates.content: Oh, I have heard—Coldstream Guards.

events.label: Holmes says he can get details from Forbes and comments on authorities and facts

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Thank you. I have no doubt I can get details from Forbes. The authorities are excellent at amassing facts, though they do not always use them to advantage.

events.label: Holmes admires a rose and walks to the open window
Holmes speaks at length about religion, deduction, and flowers

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: There is nothing in which deduction is so necessary as in religion. It can be built up as an exact science by the reasoner. Our highest assurance of the goodness of Providence seems to me to rest in the flowers. All other things, our powers our desires, our food, are all really necessary for our existence in the first instance. But this rose is an extra. Its smell and its colour are an embellishment of life, not a condition of it. It is only goodness which gives extras, and so I say again that we have much to hope from the flowers.

events.label: Percy Phelps and his nurse watch Holmes with surprise and disappointment
Holmes falls into a reverie holding the moss-rose
Miss Harrison asks whether Holmes sees any prospect of solving the mystery

communicates.speaker: miss_harrison
communicates.content: Do you see any prospect of solving this mystery, Mr. Holmes?

events.label: Holmes says he will look into the matter and report any points that strike him

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Oh, the mystery! Well, it would be absurd to deny that the case is a very abstruse and complicated one, but I can promise you that I will look into the matter and let you know any points which may strike me.

events.label: Miss Harrison asks whether Holmes sees any clue

communicates.speaker: miss_harrison
communicates.content: Do you see any clue?

events.label: Holmes says the clues furnished must be tested

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: You have furnished me with seven, but, of course, I must test them before I can pronounce upon their value.

events.label: Miss Harrison asks whether Holmes suspects someone

communicates.speaker: miss_harrison
communicates.content: You suspect some one?

events.label: Holmes says he suspects himself of coming to conclusions too rapidly

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I suspect myself. Of coming to conclusions too rapidly.

events.label: Miss Harrison advises Holmes to go to London and test his conclusions

communicates.speaker: miss_harrison
communicates.content: Then go to London and test your conclusions.

events.label: Holmes agrees with Watson and advises Phelps not to indulge false hopes

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Your advice is very excellent, Miss Harrison. I think, Watson, we cannot do better. Do not allow yourself to indulge in false hopes, Mr. Phelps. The affair is a very tangled one.

events.label: The diplomatist says he will be in a fever until he sees the others again

communicates.speaker: percival_phelps
communicates.content: I shall be in a fever until I see you again.

events.label: The diplomatist says he will come out by the same train tomorrow

communicates.speaker: percival_phelps
communicates.content: I'll come out by the same train to-morrow, though it's more than likely that my report will be a negative one.

events.label: Our client thanks the diplomatist for promising to come

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: God bless you for promising to come.

events.label: Our client says that news of action gives him fresh life

communicates.speaker: percival_phelps
communicates.content: It gives me fresh life to know that something is being done.

events.label: Our client mentions that he has received a letter from Lord Holdhurst

communicates.speaker: percival_phelps
communicates.content: By the way, I have had a letter from Lord Holdhurst.

events.label: Our client reports that Lord Holdhurst was cold but not harsh

communicates.speaker: percival_phelps
communicates.content: He was cold, but not harsh. He repeated that the matter was of the utmost importance, and added that no steps would be taken about my future—by which he means, of course, my dismissal—until my health was restored and I had an opportunity of repairing my misfortune.

events.label: Holmes says the letter was reasonable and considerate

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Well, that was reasonable and considerate.

events.label: Holmes tells Watson they will go to town for a day's work

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Come, Watson, for we have a good day's work before us in town.

events.label: Mr. Joseph Harrison drives Holmes and Watson to the station
Holmes and Watson travel by train toward Portsmouth
Holmes remarks on the London view from the train

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: It's a very cheery thing to come into London by any of these lines which run high, and allow you to look down upon the houses like this. Look at those big, isolated clumps of building rising up above the slates, like brick islands in a lead-coloured sea. The board-schools. Light-houses, my boy! Beacons of the future! Capsules with hundreds of bright little seeds in each, out of which will spring the wise, better England of the future.

events.label: Holmes asks whether Phelps drinks

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I suppose that man Phelps does not drink?

events.label: Watson replies that he should not think so

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: I should not think so.

events.label: Holmes says they must consider every possibility and describes Phelps as in deep water

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Nor should I, but we are bound to take every possibility into account. The poor devil has certainly got himself into very deep water, and it's a question whether we shall ever be able to get him ashore.

events.label: Holmes asks what Watson thought of Miss Harrison

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: What did you think of Miss Harrison?

events.label: Watson describes Miss Harrison as a girl of strong character

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: A girl of strong character.

events.label: Holmes says Miss Harrison is a good sort and describes her family

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Yes, but she is a good sort, or I am mistaken. She and her brother are the only children of an iron-master somewhere up Northumberland way. He got engaged to her when traveling last winter, and she came down to be introduced to his people, with her brother as escort. Then came the smash, and she stayed on to nurse her lover, while brother Joseph, finding himself pretty snug, stayed on too.

events.label: Holmes says he has made independent inquiries and that the day must be one of inquiries

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I've been making a few independent inquiries, you see. But to-day must be a day of inquiries.

events.label: Watson begins to mention his practice

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: My practice—

events.label: Holmes responds with asperity

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Oh, if you find your own cases more interesting than mine—

events.label: Watson says his practice can get along for a day or two

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: I was going to say that my practice could get along very well for a day or two, since it is the slackest time in the year.

events.label: Holmes agrees and says they will work on the matter together

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Excellent. Then we'll look into this matter together. I think that we should begin by seeing Forbes. He can probably tell us all the details we want until we know from what side the case is to be approached.

events.label: Watson asks whether Holmes has a clue

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: You said you had a clue?

events.label: Holmes says they have several clues and discusses possible profiting parties

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Well, we have several, but we can only test their value by further inquiry. The most difficult crime to track is the one which is purposeless. Now this is not purposeless. Who is it who profits by it? There is the French ambassador, there is the Russian, there is whoever might sell it to either of these, and there is Lord Holdhurst. Lord Holdhurst! Well, it is just conceivable that a statesman might find himself in a position where he was not sorry to have such a document accidentally destroyed.

events.label: Holmes and Watson prepare to see Lord Holdhurst and Holmes has inquiries started

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: We shall see the noble lord to-day and find out if he can tell us anything. Meanwhile I have already set inquiries on foot.

events.label: Holmes sends wires from Woking station to every evening paper in London
Holmes hands Watson a torn note-book sheet containing an advertisement
Watson asks whether the thief came in a cab and Holmes answers

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: You are confident that the thief came in a cab?

events.label: Holmes identifies the cab as one of the clues and speculates about the bell
Holmes and Watson arrive at Scotland Yard and meet Forbes
Forbes speaks frigidly to Holmes and Watson

communicates.speaker: mr_forbes
communicates.content: I've heard of your methods before now, Mr. Holmes. You are ready enough to use all the information that the police can lay at your disposal, and then you try to finish the case yourself and bring discredit on them.

events.label: Holmes replies about his recent cases and tells Forbes to work with him

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: On the contrary, out of my last fifty-three cases my name has only appeared in four, and the police have had all the credit in forty-nine. I don't blame you for not knowing this, for you are young and inexperienced, but if you wish to get on in your new duties you will work with me and not against me.

events.label: Forbes asks what steps have been taken

communicates.speaker: mr_forbes
communicates.content: I'd be very glad of a hint or two. I've certainly had no credit from the case so far. What steps have you taken?

events.label: Forbes reports that Tangey has been shadowed and comments on Tangey and his wife

communicates.speaker: mr_forbes
communicates.content: Tangey, the commissionnaire, has been shadowed. He left the Guards with a good character and we can find nothing against him. His wife is a bad lot, though. I fancy she knows more about this than appears.

events.label: Holmes asks whether Mrs. Tangey has been shadowed

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Have you shadowed her?

events.label: Forbes says a woman was set on Mrs. Tangey and got nothing from her

communicates.speaker: mr_forbes
communicates.content: We have set one of our women on to her. Mrs. Tangey drinks, and our woman has been with her twice when she was well on, but she could get nothing out of her.

events.label: Holmes and Watson leave the office and go to interview Lord Holdhurst
Holmes and Watson are shown into Lord Holdhurst's chambers
Lord Holdhurst receives Holmes and Watson courteously and seats them
Lord Holdhurst says Holmes's name is familiar and asks whose interest he represents

communicates.speaker: lord_holdhurst
communicates.content: Your name is very familiar to me, Mr. Holmes. ... In whose interest are you acting, may I ask?

events.label: Holmes says he is acting for Mr. Percy Phelps

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: In that of Mr. Percy Phelps.

events.label: Lord Holdhurst identifies Percy Phelps as his unfortunate nephew and says he cannot screen him

communicates.speaker: lord_holdhurst
communicates.content: Ah, my unfortunate nephew! You can understand that our kinship makes it the more impossible for me to screen him in any way. I fear that the incident must have a very prejudicial effect upon his career.

events.label: Holmes asks whether the document will change matters if it is found

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: But if the document is found?

events.label: Lord Holdhurst says he will give any information in his power

communicates.speaker: lord_holdhurst
communicates.content: I shall be happy to give you any information in my power.

events.label: Holmes asks whether the instructions for copying the document were given in the room

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Was it in this room that you gave your instructions as to the copying of the document?

events.label: Holmes and Watson travel to Woking together
Holmes reports that his inquiry has yielded no result and that he has seen Forbes and Percy Phelps's uncle

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: My report, as I expected, is a negative one. I have seen Forbes, and I have seen your uncle, and I have set one or two trains of inquiry upon foot which may lead to something.

events.label: Holmes speaks with Lord Holdhurst about the treaty and the thief

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Did you ever mention to any one that it was your intention to give any one the treaty to be copied? There is another very important point which I wish to discuss with you. You feared, as I understand, that very grave results might follow from the details of this treaty becoming known. If the treaty had reached, let us say, the French or Russian Foreign Office, you would expect to hear of it? Since nearly ten weeks have elapsed, then, and nothing has been heard, it is not unfair to suppose that for some reason the treaty has not reached them. Perhaps he is waiting for a better price. If he waits a little longer he will get no price at all. The treaty will cease to be secret in a few months. Of course, it is a possible supposition that the thief has had a sudden illness. I did not say so.

events.label: Lord Holdhurst answers Holmes's questions and bows the visitors out

communicates.speaker: lord_holdhurst
communicates.content: Never. Absolutely. Very grave results indeed. Not yet. I should. We can hardly suppose, Mr. Holmes, that the thief took the treaty in order to frame it and hang it up. An attack of brain-fever, for example? Every success to your investigation, be the criminal who it may.

events.label: Holmes and Watson go to see Percy Phelps at Briarbrae, Woking
Percy Phelps asks whether there is any news

communicates.speaker: percival_phelps
communicates.content: Any news?

events.label: Phelps says he has more to tell than his visitors have for him

communicates.speaker: percival_phelps
communicates.content: We have more to tell you than you have for us.

events.label: Phelps sits down on the couch
Phelps reports an adventure during the night

communicates.speaker: percival_phelps
communicates.content: We have had an adventure during the night, and one which might have proved to be a serious one.

events.label: Phelps describes a fear of conspiracy and attack on his life and honour

communicates.speaker: percival_phelps
communicates.content: I begin to believe that I am the unconscious centre of some monstrous conspiracy, and that my life is aimed at as well as my honour.

events.label: Holmes asks Phelps to hear the account

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Pray let me hear it.

events.label: Phelps says he slept without a nurse in the room for the first time

communicates.speaker: percival_phelps
communicates.content: Last night was the very first night that I have ever slept without a nurse in the room. I was so much better that I thought I could dispense with one.

events.label: Phelps says he had a night-light burning

communicates.speaker: percival_phelps
communicates.content: I had a night-light burning.

events.label: Phelps hears a slight noise and listens
Phelps hears a metallic snick from the window
Phelps sits up in amazement
An instrument is forced through the slit between the sashes and the catch is pressed back
A pause lasts about ten minutes while the intruder waits
The window is slowly opened
Phelps springs out of bed and opens the shutters
Phelps sees a man crouching at the window
The man flees from the window
The man is wrapped in a cloak covering the lower part of his face
The man holds a weapon in his hand
Holmes says the account is most interesting and asks what Phelps did next

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: This is most interesting. Pray what did you do then?

events.label: Phelps would have followed the intruder through the open window if stronger
Phelps rings the bell and rouses the house
Phelps shouts and Joseph comes down and rouses the others
Joseph and the groom find marks on the bed outside the window
Joseph and the groom fail to follow the trail across the grass because the weather has been dry
A place on the wooden fence shows signs that someone got over it and snapped the top rail
Phelps says he has not yet told the local police

communicates.speaker: percival_phelps
communicates.content: I have said nothing to the local police yet, for I thought I had best have your opinion first.

events.label: Holmes rises and paces about the room in excitement
Phelps smiles and remarks that misfortunes never come single

communicates.speaker: percival_phelps
communicates.content: Misfortunes never come single.

events.label: Holmes says Phelps has had his share

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: You have certainly had your share.

events.label: Phelps asks whether the others can walk round the house with him

communicates.speaker: percival_phelps
communicates.content: Do you think you could walk round the house with me?

events.label: Miss Harrison says she would like sunshine and that Joseph will come too

communicates.speaker: miss_harrison
communicates.content: Oh, yes, I should like a little sunshine. Joseph will come, too.

events.label: Holmes declines to let Miss Harrison come and instructs her to remain sitting

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I am afraid not. I think I must ask you to remain sitting exactly where you are.

events.label: Miss Harrison resumes her seat displeased
The group sets off together
The group passes round the lawn to the outside of the bedroom window
Holmes examines the blurred marks on the bed
Holmes says no one could make much of the marks

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I don't think any one could make much of this.

events.label: Holmes suggests going round the house to see why the burglar chose the room

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Let us go round the house and see why this particular room was chosen by the burglar. I should have thought those larger windows of the drawing-room and dining-room would have had more attractions for him.

events.label: Joseph Harrison suggests the larger windows are more visible from the road

communicates.speaker: joseph_harrison
communicates.content: They are more visible from the road.

events.label: Holmes asks about a door and what it is for

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Ah, yes, of course. There is a door here which he might have attempted. What is it for?

events.label: Joseph Harrison explains that the side entrance is for trades-people and is locked at night

communicates.speaker: joseph_harrison
communicates.content: It is the side entrance for trades-people. Of course it is locked at night.

events.label: Holmes asks whether the house has ever had an alarm like this before

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Have you ever had an alarm like this before?

events.label: Phelps answers that there has never been one

communicates.speaker: percival_phelps
communicates.content: Never.

events.label: Holmes asks whether plate or anything valuable is kept in the house

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Do you keep plate in the house, or anything to attract burglars?

events.label: Phelps answers that there is nothing of value

communicates.speaker: percival_phelps
communicates.content: Nothing of value.

events.label: Holmes strolled round the house in an unusual negligent manner
Holmes asks Joseph Harrison about the place where the intruder scaled the fence

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: By the way, you found some place, I understand, where the fellow scaled the fence. Let us have a look at that!

events.label: Joseph Harrison leads the group to the cracked fence rail
Holmes removes and examines the hanging wood fragment
Holmes asks whether the damage was done last night and says it looks old

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Do you think that was done last night? It looks rather old, does it not?

events.label: Holmes notes that there are no marks of anyone jumping down on the other side and turns back
Percy Phelps walks slowly while leaning on his future brother-in-law's arm
Holmes reaches the open bedroom window before the others
Holmes orders Miss Harrison to stay where she is all day and to lock the bedroom door on the outside at bedtime

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Miss Harrison, you must stay where you are all day. Let nothing prevent you from staying where you are all day. It is of the utmost importance. When you go to bed lock the door of this room on the outside and keep the key. Promise to do this. He will come to London with us. It is for his sake. You can serve him. Quick! Promise!

events.label: Miss Harrison assents with a nod
Joseph Harrison asks Annie why she is moping and invites her into the sunshine

communicates.speaker: joseph_harrison
communicates.content: Why do you sit moping there, Annie? Come out into the sunshine!

events.label: Miss Harrison refuses and says the room is cool and soothing

communicates.speaker: miss_harrison
communicates.content: No, thank you, Joseph. I have a slight headache and this room is deliciously cool and soothing.

events.label: Holmes asks Phelps to come up to London with them

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: It would be a very great help to me if you would come up to London with us.

events.label: Holmes proposes that Phelps stay there to-night

communicates.speaker: mr_phelps
communicates.content: Perhaps you would like me to stay there to-night?

events.label: Holmes arranges for Watson to look after Phelps

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: My friend Watson is a medical man, you know, and he'll look after you.

events.label: The group has lunch at the house before setting off for town
Miss Harrison excuses herself from leaving the bedroom
Holmes escorts Watson and Phelps to the station and into their carriage
Holmes announces that he does not intend to leave Woking

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I have no intention of leaving Woking.

events.label: Holmes asks Watson to drive to Baker Street with their friend and remain with him

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: When you reach London you would oblige me by driving at once to Baker Street with our friend here, and remaining with him until I see you again.

events.label: Phelps asks about the London investigation

communicates.speaker: mr_phelps
communicates.content: But how about our investigation in London?

events.label: Holmes says the London investigation can be done tomorrow

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: We can do that to-morrow. I think that just at present I can be of more immediate use here.

events.label: Phelps asks Holmes to tell people at Briarbrae that he hopes to return tomorrow night

communicates.speaker: mr_phelps
communicates.content: You might tell them at Briarbrae that I hope to be back to-morrow night.

events.label: Holmes says he hardly expects to go back to Briarbrae

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I hardly expect to go back to Briarbrae.

events.label: Phelps and Watson discuss Holmes's conduct during the journey
Phelps proposes that the burglary involved a burglar and not an ordinary thief

communicates.speaker: mr_phelps
communicates.content: I suppose he wants to find out some clue as to the burglary last night, if a burglar it was. For myself, I don't believe it was an ordinary thief.

events.label: Phelps states that he believes a political intrigue is directed against him

communicates.speaker: mr_phelps
communicates.content: Upon my word, you may put it down to my weak nerves or not, but I believe there is some deep political intrigue going on around me, and that for some reason that passes my understanding my life is aimed at by the conspirators. It sounds high-flown and absurd, but consider the facts! Why should a thief try to break in at a bedroom window, where there could be no hope of any plunder, and why should he come with a long knife in his hand?

events.label: Watson asks whether the intruder used a house-breaker's jimmy

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: You are sure it was not a house-breaker's jimmy?

events.label: Watson says he has seen Holmes do remarkable things

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: I have seen him do some remarkable things.

events.label: Watson says he has known Holmes solve questions with fewer clues

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: I have known him solve questions which presented fewer clues than yours.

events.label: Watson says Holmes has acted on behalf of three reigning houses of Europe

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: To my certain knowledge he has acted on behalf of three of the reigning houses of Europe in very vital matters.

events.label: Phelps asks whether Holmes is hopeful

communicates.speaker: percival_phelps
communicates.content: But you know him well, Watson. He is such an inscrutable fellow that I never quite know what to make of him. Do you think he is hopeful? Do you think he expects to make a success of it?

events.label: Watson says Holmes has said nothing

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: He has said nothing.

events.label: Phelps says Holmes is taciturn when on a scent

communicates.speaker: percival_phelps
communicates.content: That is a bad sign. On the contrary, I have noticed that when he is off the trail he generally says so. It is when he is on a scent and is not quite absolutely sure yet that it is the right one that he is most taciturn.

events.label: Watson urges Phelps to go to bed and be fresh for tomorrow

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: Now, my dear fellow, we can't help matters by making ourselves nervous about them, so let me implore you to go to bed and so be fresh for whatever may await us to-morrow.

events.label: Watson persuades Phelps to take his advice and go to bed
Watson lies awake brooding over the problem
Watson wakes and goes to Phelps's room
Phelps asks whether Holmes has arrived

communicates.speaker: percival_phelps
communicates.content: whether Holmes had arrived yet.

events.label: Watson says Holmes will arrive when promised

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: He'll be here when he promised, and not an instant sooner or later.

events.label: A hansom arrives at the door and Watson's friend gets out
Watson and Phelps see Holmes's bandaged left hand and pale face
Holmes enters the house and comes upstairs later
Phelps says Holmes looks like a beaten man

communicates.speaker: percival_phelps
communicates.content: He looks like a beaten man.

events.label: Watson says the clue probably lies in town

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: After all, the clue of the matter lies probably here in town.

events.label: Phelps groans
Phelps says he had hoped for much from Holmes's return and asks what can be the matter

communicates.speaker: percival_phelps
communicates.content: I don't know how it is, but I had hoped for so much from his return. But surely his hand was not tied up like that yesterday. What can be the matter?

events.label: Watson asks Holmes whether he is wounded

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: You are not wounded, Holmes?

events.label: Holmes says his injury is only a scratch from his own clumsiness

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Tut, it is only a scratch through my own clumsiness.

events.label: Holmes describes Phelps's case as one of the darkest he has investigated

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: This case of yours, Mr. Phelps, is certainly one of the darkest which I have ever investigated.

events.label: Holmes says the experience was remarkable

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: It has been a most remarkable experience.

events.label: Watson remarks that the bandage tells of adventures and asks Holmes to explain what happened

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: That bandage tells of adventures. Won't you tell us what has happened?

events.label: Holmes postpones the explanation until after breakfast

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: After breakfast, my dear Watson. Remember that I have breathed thirty miles of Surrey air this morning.

events.label: Holmes asks whether his cabman advertisement has received no answer and comments on failure

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I suppose that there has been no answer from my cabman advertisement? Well, well, we cannot expect to score every time.

events.label: Mrs. Hudson brings tea, coffee, and breakfast covers to the table
Holmes praises Mrs. Hudson's breakfast and asks Watson what food he has

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Mrs. Hudson has risen to the occasion. Her cuisine is a little limited, but she has as good an idea of breakfast as a Scotch-woman. What have you here, Watson?

events.label: Watson answers that he has ham and eggs

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: Ham and eggs.

events.label: Holmes invites Phelps to take breakfast food

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Good! What are you going to take, Mr. Phelps—curried fowl or eggs, or will you help yourself?

events.label: Phelps refuses food

communicates.speaker: percival_phelps
communicates.content: Thank you. I can eat nothing. Thank you, I would really rather not.

events.label: Holmes suggests that Phelps help him instead

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Oh, come! Try the dish before you. Well, then, I suppose that you have no objection to helping me?

events.label: Phelps raises a cover, screams, stares at the dish, and sees a blue-grey paper cylinder
Phelps seizes the cylinder, reacts with delight, and collapses into an armchair
Holmes soothes and pats Phelps on the shoulder

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: There! there! It was too bad to spring it on you like this, but Watson here will tell you that I never can resist a touch of the dramatic.

events.label: Phelps thanks Holmes and says he has saved his honour

communicates.speaker: percival_phelps
communicates.content: God bless you! You have saved my honour.

events.label: Holmes says his own honour was at stake and that failing is hateful to him

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Well, my own was at stake, you know. I assure you it is just as hateful to me to fail in a case as it can be to you to blunder over a commission.

events.label: Phelps puts the document into his coat pocket
Phelps says he is dying to know how Holmes got the document and where it was

communicates.speaker: percival_phelps
communicates.content: I have not the heart to interrupt your breakfast any further, and yet I am dying to know how you got it and where it was.

events.label: Sherlock Holmes eats and drinks breakfast
Sherlock Holmes rises, lights his pipe, and settles into his chair
Sherlock Holmes explains his movements before arriving at Briarbrae

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I'll tell you what I did first, and how I came to do it afterwards. After leaving you at the station I went for a charming walk through some admirable Surrey scenery to a pretty little village called Ripley, where I had my tea at an inn, and took the precaution of filling my flask and of putting a paper of sandwiches in my pocket. There I remained until evening, when I set off for Woking again, and found myself in the high-road outside Briarbrae just after sunset. I waited until the road was clear and then I clambered over the fence into the grounds.

events.label: Sherlock Holmes enters the grounds by climbing over the fence
Phelps reacts to Holmes's mention of the gate being open

communicates.speaker: percival_phelps
communicates.content: Surely the gate was open!

events.label: Sherlock Holmes uses the fir-trees as cover and crawls to the rhododendrons
Sherlock Holmes observes Miss Harrison reading in the room
Miss Harrison closes her book, fastens the shutters, and retires
Sherlock Holmes hears the door shut and infers the key was turned in the lock
Phelps responds about the key

communicates.speaker: percival_phelps
communicates.content: The key!

events.label: Holmes explains that he instructed Miss Harrison to lock the door outside and take the key

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I had given Miss Harrison instructions to lock the door on the outside and take the key with her when she went to bed. She carried out every one of my injunctions to the letter.

events.label: Miss Harrison departs and the lights go out
Holmes waits in the rhododendron bush through the night
Mr. Joseph Harrison opens the servants' door and steps into the moonlight
Phelps reacts to the name Joseph Harrison

communicates.speaker: percival_phelps
communicates.content: Joseph!

events.label: Joseph Harrison conceals his face with a black coat while moving to the window
Joseph Harrison opens the window and the shutters with a knife
Joseph Harrison lights the candles and turns back the carpet
Joseph Harrison removes the board and draws out the paper cylinder
Joseph Harrison blows out the candles and walks into Holmes's arms
Holmes describes Joseph Harrison as attacking with a knife and being subdued

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Well, he has rather more viciousness than I gave him credit for, has Master Joseph. He flew at me with his knife, and I had to grasp him twice, and got a cut over the knuckles, before I had the upper hand of him. He looked murder out of the only eye he could see with when we had finished, but he listened to reason and gave up the papers.

events.label: Holmes lets Joseph Harrison go and wires full particulars to Forbes
Holmes says the stolen papers may be recovered before Joseph Harrison reaches the place

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: If he is quick enough to catch his bird, well and good. But if, as I shrewdly suspect, he finds the nest empty before he gets there, why, all the better for the government.

events.label: Holmes says Lord Holdhurst and Percy Phelps would prefer the affair not reach a police-court

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I fancy that Lord Holdhurst for one, and Mr. Percy Phelps for another, would very much rather that the affair never got as far as a police-court.

events.label: Percy Phelps reacts in shock
Holmes explains that Joseph Harrison stole the treaty papers from the Foreign Office room

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Hum! I am afraid Joseph's character is a rather deeper and more dangerous one than one might judge from his appearance. From what I have heard from him this morning, I gather that he has lost heavily in dabbling with stocks, and that he is ready to do anything on earth to better his fortunes. Being an absolutely selfish man, when a chance presented itself he did not allow either his sister's happiness or your reputation to hold his hand. The principal difficulty in your case lay in the fact of there being too much evidence. What was vital was overlaid and hidden by what was irrelevant. Of all the facts which were presented to us we had to pick just those which we deemed to be essential, and then piece them together in their order, so as to reconstruct this very remarkable chain of events. I had already begun to suspect Joseph, from the fact that you had intended to travel home with him that night, and that therefore it was a likely enough thing that he should call for you, knowing the Foreign Office well, upon his way. When I heard that some one had been so anxious to get into the bedroom, in which no one but Joseph could have concealed anything—you told us in your narrative how you had turned Joseph out when you arrived with the doctor—my suspicions all changed to certainties, especially as the attempt was made on the first night upon which the nurse was absent, showing that the intruder was well acquainted with the ways of the house. The facts of the case, as far as I have worked them out, are these: this Joseph Harrison entered the office through the Charles Street door, and knowing his way he walked straight into your room the instant after you left it. Finding no one there he promptly rang the bell, and at the instant that he did so his eyes caught the paper upon the table. A glance showed him that chance had put in his way a State document of immense value, and in an instant he had thrust it into his pocket and was gone. A few minutes elapsed, as you remember, before the sleepy commissionnaire drew your attention to the bell, and those were just enough to give the thief time to make his escape.

events.label: A man travels to Woking by the first train and hides his booty in a safe place
A man plans to take the booty to the French embassy or another place offering a long price
There is a sudden return

He thinks he sees his chance
He tries to steal in but is baffled
Watson and Holmes discuss the unusual draught

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: You remember that you did not take your usual draught that night.

events.label: Holmes states that the draught had been made efficacious and relied on unconsciousness

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I fancy that he had taken steps to make that draught efficacious, and that he quite relied upon your being unconscious. Of course, I understood that he would repeat the attempt whenever it could be done with safety.

events.label: Watson leaves the room and gives him the chance he wanted
Holmes keeps Miss Harrison in the room all day

Holmes keeps Miss Harrison in the room and guards it to prevent anticipation
Holmes lets him take the papers from the hiding-place
Phelps asks why he tried the window on the first occasion

communicates.speaker: percival_phelps
communicates.content: Why did he try the window on the first occasion, when he might have entered by the door?

events.label: Holmes explains that reaching the door would require passing seven bedrooms and that the lawn could be reached with ease

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: In reaching the door he would have to pass seven bedrooms. On the other hand, he could get out on to the lawn with ease.

events.label: Phelps asks whether he had murderous intention and says the knife was only meant as a tool

communicates.speaker: percival_phelps
communicates.content: You do not think that he had any murderous intention? The knife was only meant as a tool.

events.label: Holmes answers that the matter may be so and refuses to trust Mr. Joseph Harrison's mercy

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: It may be so. I can only say for certain that Mr. Joseph Harrison is a gentleman to whose mercy I should be extremely unwilling to trust.

clues.significance: Holmes inferred that the writing was a woman's from the letter he read.
Watson found that the original treaty had been taken from the desk while the copy remained behind.
Watson found no footmark outline on the corridor's creamy linoleum, which showed impressions very easily.
Holmes used the note-book sheet as an advertised clue to obtain the number of the cab that had dropped a fare near the Foreign Office at about quarter to ten on May 23rd.
Holmes treated the bell as the most distinctive feature of the case and framed competing explanations for why it rang.
Percival Phelps inferred that the intruder carried a weapon and that it looked like a long knife from the gleam he saw as the man turned to run.
Holmes inferred that the marks on the bed were hopelessly blurred and vague and that they would not provide much help.
Holmes inferred that the cracked rail looked rather old and that the damage had probably not been done last night.
Holmes recovered the little cylinder of paper from the hiding-place in the room.

Holmes inferred that Joseph Harrison stole the State document from Percy Phelps's room after entering through the Charles Street door, ringing the bell, spotting the paper on the table, and pocketing it before the commissionnaire noticed.
